newsitem.title: USA: US Feb spot natgas down $1 or more from Jan index.
newsitem.headline: US Feb spot natgas down $1 or more from Jan index.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for February delivery settled $1 or more under January indices Wednesday, as more moderate weather was forecast for most of the U.S. by week's end, sources said.
February 1 prices on the Gulf Coast pipes were mostly in the $2.84-2.89 per mmBtu range, falling about $1 under January indices.
Sources attributed the sharp decline in prices to milder weather and a significant build in storage inventories.
Gulf prices for Thursday delivery were mostly steady in the $2.95-3.05 range.
In the Midcontinent, February 1 prices slumped about $1.50 below January indices to the $2.70-2.75 range, as forecasters called for mostly normal temperatures in the first week of February.
Midcontinent prices for Thursday followed the February market downward as traders reported closing most deals around $2.80, down about 20 cents from Tuesday.
In west Texas, Permian prices for Feb 1 fell by an average of $1.60 below January indices to the $2.55-2.60 range. Swing prices were also softer around $2.70.

February prices at the southern California border hovered in the low-$2.60s, down about $1.70 from January's index levels. Swing prices drifted into the high-$2.50s, traders said, down about 40 cents from Tuesday.
In the East, February prices at the New York city-gate were about $3.60, while Thursday gas sold mostly in the $3.80-3.85 range.
